items.title: Nvidia enters life without Jensen Huang
items.content:
Read Online | Sign Up | Advertise

Good morning, {{ first_name | AI enthusiasts }}, and welcome to our 4,207 new readers. Two weeks ago, a NYT report tied Nvidia’s CEO to an alleged Chinese intelligence asset. Now, the man who turned a Denny’s-booth startup into the engine of the AI boom is out the door.

Jensen Huang has resigned after a 33-year run at Nvidia, leaving the world’s most important AI infrastructure company without its founder, and without a clear plan for what comes next.

In today’s AI rundown:

  • Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia’s CEO

  • Rowan’s Corner: How I use AI to coach my calls

  • Build a shared tracker in Claude Sheets

  • Google joins the race for your face with AI glasses

LATEST DEVELOPMENTS

NVIDIA

🚨 Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia’s CEO

Image source: Nvidia / The Rundown

The Rundown: Jensen Huang just resigned as Nvidia’s CEO and board member, effective immediately, after reports of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset; CFO Colette Kress has been named interim CEO.

The details:

  • The exit came days after Huang admitted to infidelity following reports linking him to an alleged Chinese spy. The board backed him, saying it had “no reason to believe” national security or company secrets were compromised.

  • Pressure built after the NYT reported a second relationship with an Nvidia executive; Reuters reported a third with another employee after the resignation.

  • Kress, CFO since 2013, will hold both roles as the board looks for a replacement, with Trump pitching Tim Cook as the “only one man” who could take the job.

  • Nvidia closed down 4% Thursday after falling more than 14%, with earnings due Nov. 17 and House committee chairs seeking a closed-door briefing from Huang.

Why it matters: Over 33 years, Huang made Nvidia the company it is, taking it from gaming GPUs to the hardware behind modern AI. Under him, it stayed dominant even as rivals pushed their own chips. Whoever steps into his shoes will have to build on that and decide which of his fights to keep, from lighter AI regulation to chip sales to China.

TOGETHER WITH HUBSPOT

🧠 100+ ChatGPT prompts to revolutionize your workflow

The Rundown: HubSpot’s free, comprehensive “How to Use ChatGPT at Work” guide provides 100+ ready-to-use prompts to help professionals boost efficiency and adopt AI-driven workflows.

Inside, you’ll find:

  • Quick crash course to master ChatGPT in under 30 minutes

  • Practical industry use cases to spark real-world inspiration

  • 100+ prompts to streamline tasks and accelerate productivity

  • Expert tips to tackle common AI roadblocks with confidence

Get your free copy.

ROWAN’S CORNER

📞 How I use AI to coach my calls

Screenshot via Forbes interview with Rowan

Rowan: After every high-stakes call, I let AI tear apart my performance. It started as a weird quirk several months ago, and it’s quietly become one of my most useful habits, so I figured it’s worth sharing.

The setup is simple. I record my meetings with Granola (you could use any meeting note taker), connect the transcripts to Claude, and instead of just pulling summaries and action items, I make it look backward at my own performance.

A few of the analyses I run:

  • My talk ratio on sales calls, flagged whenever it passes 50% (typically you want to talk less)

  • Every moment I dodged a hard topic or put off a decision I could’ve made on the spot

  • A commitment log of everything promised, including every “let me think about it,” which gets pushed into my to-do lists

  • An objection library of every pushback partners raised this year, with a stronger answer drafted for each

One quick tip if you try this is to ask for exact quotes, so Claude or ChatGPT puts your own words next to what you should’ve said.

And this works for way more than my calls. You could run the same workflow on recruiting calls, sales calls, leadership meetings, heck, even podcasts and interview recordings. If it’s recorded, it can coach you.

AI TRAINING

💻️ Build a shared tracker in Claude Sheets

The Rundown: Claude now builds its own spreadsheets, turning a description into a table and leaving the formulas in the cells, so you can check every number. In this guide, you’ll build a campaign tracker with status and budget, then share it for editing.

Step-by-step:

  1. Go to claude.ai/artifacts, click the green Sheets tile under Make something new, and describe the tracker: every column, dropdown values, and cells with formulas

  2. Click a total and read the formula bar. Then select the table, click Ask Claude, and ask it to point out any cell holding a typed number instead of a formula, since only formulas update when Spent changes

  3. Ask Claude to highlight tasks that are past their due date and not Done. Then paste your own tasks over the samples and have Claude delete the leftovers

  4. Click Share, invite a teammate with Can edit, and leave General access on Only you. On paid plans, people can edit cells but can’t ask Claude for changes

Pro tip: Before any big change, open Share, then the Export tab, and download an Excel copy. If an edit goes wrong, you still have the tracker as it was. For a bad build, Undo on the “Claude updated” notice takes the whole thing back.

Watch the full guide at The Rundown University →

PRESENTED BY INCOGNI

📞 That scam call wasn’t random

The Rundown: Scammers don’t guess your number — they buy it from data brokers selling your phone, home address, and relatives’ info online. That’s how a random call turns into phishing, impersonation, or worse. Incogni removes your data from these databases and keeps removing it automatically.

With Incogni working in the background, you can:

  • Keep phone numbers and addresses off broker databases

  • Reduce exposure to identity theft and impersonation

  • Let automated removals do the work continuously

Get 58% off with the code RUNDOWN.

GOOGLE

👓️ Google joins the race for your face with AI glasses

Image source: Google

The Rundown: Google opened pre-orders for its first Gemini-powered AI smart glasses, 18 months after announcing them at I/O 2025, with frames from Warby Parker and Gentle Monster starting at $395 in a direct challenge to Meta’s Ray-Bans.

The details:

  • Built with Samsung, the nine styles pack a 12MP camera, open-ear speakers, and up to nine hours of battery into 41-gram frames, with no display in the lenses.

  • Wearers can say “Hey Gemini” to ask about what they’re looking at, get Maps directions in their ear, play music, or translate speech live across 70+ languages.

  • Google says the glasses redact bystanders’ faces before Gemini sees them, show a light when recording, and stop recording if the light is covered; users can even control which apps access the camera and mic.

  • They go on sale Dec. 10 in the U.S. and South Korea and work with iPhones too, taking on Meta, which shipped 81% of AI glasses in the first half of the year.

Why it matters: Meta holds the crown in AI glasses, but privacy backlash over their cameras has dogged it, to the point it launched a camera-free model in September. With its new glasses and their added privacy features, Google is pitching itself as the safer pick, betting it can keep the camera and still earn the trust Meta has struggled to win.

COMMUNITY AI WORKFLOW OF THE DAY

▸ A Rundown reader used AI to turn personal stories into published books

Today’s workflow comes from an anonymous Rundown reader:

“After retiring from medicine, I began writing personal stories and used ChatGPT to polish them for sharing. Over time, it helped me connect stories, identify larger themes, and explore new ideas. I bring my own stories, reflections, and questions, then work with ChatGPT through suggestions, revisions, and sometimes disagreements. I also use Claude and Gemini as independent reviewers to catch weaknesses or missed possibilities, while keeping all creative and editorial decisions my own.

This process has helped me publish books and create Creating Space, a collection of contemplative resources for individuals and groups. Each project sparks new questions and ideas. The biggest benefit hasn’t been saving time. At 73, I’ve begun to see myself as a creator, using AI to explore possibilities and bring my ideas to life while retaining responsibility for the work.”

items.title: AI’s biggest CEO may be on his way out
items.content:
Read Online | Sign Up | Advertise

Good morning, {{ first_name | AI enthusiasts }}, and welcome to our 5,952 new readers. Jensen Huang has been Nvidia’s center of gravity since 1993, long enough to turn it into the engine of the entire AI boom. That run may suddenly be down to its final days.

A new report says directors are preparing to push the co-founder out as CEO, hours after a second affair surfaced, this one with an executive who reports to him. As crazy as it would’ve sounded a few weeks ago, Nvidia without Jensen is no longer unthinkable.

Reminder: Our next live workshop is today at 2 PM EST — join Nate Grahek for a free tour of the new all-in-one Claude and the underrated features most users are still missing. RSVP here.

In today’s AI rundown:

  • Jensen Huang’s job in doubt after second affair report

  • Nate’s Notebook: Claude Projects now take their own notes

  • Claim and set up your business on ChatGPT

  • Google’s new AlphaGenome traces disease to cells

LATEST DEVELOPMENTS

NVIDIA

🚪 Jensen Huang’s job in doubt after second affair report

Image source: Creative Commons / The Rundown

The Rundown: Nvidia’s directors are preparing to remove Jensen Huang as CEO, according to The Wall Street Journal, just hours after The New York Times reported a second affair for the co-founder — this time with a vice president who answers to him.

The details:

  • Five people who’ve worked at Nvidia told the NYT that Jensen and Kimberly Powell, its health care VP, had an affair that’s been discussed internally.

  • Jensen’s security reportedly offered an NDA after someone filmed the two being ‘affectionate’ during a March conference, though the NYT hasn’t seen the video.

  • The Economist called for Jensen to resign for his involvement with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang, with members of Congress also pushing for his exit.

  • Nvidia lost over $427B in market value in two sessions after the affair came out, rose Wednesday, then fell about 8% after hours as the two reports landed.

Why it matters: Nvidia ranks among the world’s biggest companies; its chips train nearly every major AI, and almost all of that runs through Jensen. With roughly 60 direct reports and a rockstar persona that customers treat as the company’s face, there’s no playbook for replacing him — and a major shock to the system may be incoming.

TOGETHER WITH PLAID

🔌 Plaid powers Finances in ChatGPT

The Rundown: Plaid’s secure, permissioned data access gives ChatGPT the financial context it needs to give people personalized answers to their money questions. Hear from Ethan Bloch, OpenAI’s Product Lead, Personal Finance, on why secure connectivity and financial context are foundational to the experience.

When users connect their financial accounts using Plaid, they can ask:

  • “Which subscriptions should I cancel?”

  • “What would a big trip do to my savings?”

  • “Am I being double-charged?”

Read the full story.

NATE’S NOTEBOOK

🗂️ Claude Projects now take their own notes

The Rundown: Each week, Rundown AI educator Nate Grahek breaks down what he’s seeing while teaching real teams to use AI.

Nate: Claude Projects on the web can now save their own knowledge files. It went seemingly unnoticed, and I think it matters more than any demo you saw this week.

You know the demos: Fable 5.2 had 1,000 agents build an entire operating system in eight days. That’s good for clicks, but it doesn’t apply to getting real work done.

What gets real work done is context. For three years, I’ve taught that Claude needs to know the way you do the work, in your role, at your organization. Set up a Project once with the documents that show how you do a proposal the right way, and it reuses them over and over. On the web, that Project works on any of your devices, and you can share it with your team.

The catch was that Claude couldn’t add to it. If you wanted Claude to save its research and compare it against next week’s, you had to work locally, and that closed the door on your phone and easy sharing.

Now, Claude can do the research, synthesize the main ideas, and save them as new knowledge files in the Project. Put it on a schedule, and it’s gathering and curating its own knowledge, both inside and outside your organization.

Projects have long been Claude’s killer feature, and one tiny detail just made them even better.

P.S. — If you’re interested in learning about how to utilize Claude to its full potential, join me at today’s free workshop.

AI TRAINING

✅ Claim and set up your business on ChatGPT

The Rundown: When someone asks ChatGPT about a business like yours, the answer can now draw on details you control. In this guide, you’ll claim your business in ChatGPT Business Hub, verify it, fix what ChatGPT shows, and see how people find you.

Step-by-step:

  1. Open Business Hub from the ChatGPT sidebar and search for your business. For now, local stores and restaurants can only claim an existing US listing

  2. Prove it’s yours with a code sent to the business phone or email, a DNS record on your domain, or your Shopify store. Use whichever option you’re shown

  3. Complete Persona’s ID check with your government ID and registration details. Edits, insights, and the blue check all wait on Persona’s approval

  4. Update your description, contact, and policies. OpenAI reviews each change before it appears, and ChatGPT may also use your website, so keep it current

  5. Open Insights to see mentions, views, and clicks. Eligible US online businesses can also build a business agent; test it in the preview before publishing

Pro tip: Persona checks your details against official records. Copy your legal name, address, and registration number into a note and paste from there. Typing from memory is how an old address slips in.

Watch the full guide at The Rundown University →

PRESENTED BY ARCHERA

💰 Insurance Backed Guarantee for your cloud spend

The Rundown: Unpredictable AI workloads make long-term cloud commitments feel like a gamble. Archera lets you commit with a one-time 30-day minimum, then keep or remove the commitment anytime after. If usage drops, an Insurance Backed Guarantee pays you cash back.

With Archera, you get:

  • Commitment discounts and in-demand capacity across AWS, Azure, and GCP

  • Cash back on unused commitments through an Insurance Backed Guarantee

  • A free FinOps agent and commitment automation

See your savings without the lock-in.

GOOGLE DEEPMIND

🔬 Google’s new AlphaGenome traces disease to cells

Image source: Google DeepMind

The Rundown: DeepMind released AlphaGenome 2, an AI that predicts how small DNA differences between people play out inside specific cell types — a more detailed view than the original that could help trace diseases back to the cell types involved.

The details:

  • DeepMind’s Adam Gayoso called it “tying human genetics to cell biology,” as the original version averaged whole tissues while version 2 studies each cell type.

  • The original caught just 16% of the DNA changes behind gene shifts in a test on 28 immune cell types, with AlphaGenome 2 nearly doubling it to 30%.

  • Labs can also hand it gene activity from just a few dozen cells, like immune cells fired up by a vaccine, and get predictions without having to retrain the model.

  • Tested on inflammatory bowel disease, the model matched a recent study by picking out a DNA change that overworks one gene in the gut’s immune cells.

Why it matters: Scientists have found plenty of DNA quirks tied to diseases like type 2 diabetes, but they often can’t tell which cells they actually impact — the part drug makers need. AlphaGenome 2 helps answer that question and identify the experiments worth running first, which could mean better-aimed treatments for common illnesses.

COMMUNITY AI WORKFLOW OF THE DAY

▸ Arun built an AI badminton coach that narrates match reviews

Today’s workflow comes from reader Arun Sriraman:

“I use this workflow to turn a recording of a badminton match into a coaching session for individual players. It's for coaches and players who want written and spoken feedback on a specific player’s performance without writing the analysis from scratch.

Share the analysis output with an LLM such as Gemini or Claude and ask it to turn the output into a human-sounding coaching narrative. Convert the narrative to speech with TTS, then video encode the coaching session.

The end result is a narrated coaching session video for the player under review, ready to share with them.”

items.title: OpenAI invites brands to set up shop in ChatGPT
items.content:
Read Online | Sign Up | Advertise

Good morning, {{ first_name | AI enthusiasts }}, and welcome to our 5,653 new readers. Google conditioned companies to obsess over their search listings for decades. That same scramble has been playing out on AI platforms, and OpenAI just gave brands an official way in.

Its new ‘Businesses’ beta gives brands a verified profile, a view of their mentions, and a personalized AI agent for direct buyer questions, opening a new way to meet customers where they’re increasingly searching… inside ChatGPT.

In today’s AI rundown:

  • OpenAI invites brands to set up shop in ChatGPT

  • Anthropic stretches Claude across the office

  • Put your open Chrome tabs to work with AI

  • ‘AI 2027’ authors move up their timelines

LATEST DEVELOPMENTS

OPENAI

🛒 OpenAI invites brands to set up shop in ChatGPT

Image source: OpenAI

The Rundown: OpenAI just introduced Businesses in ChatGPT, a beta hub where brands can claim a verified profile, track how often the chatbot mentions them, and set up AI agents for shoppers, which paid ads can now point to.

The details:

  • Profiles are currently free to claim for eligible companies, while agents are live first for U.S. online retailers and digital service firms.

  • Brands can write their agent’s instructions and add product details, with shoppers opening it from the profile in a labeled chat separate from ChatGPT’s answers.

  • A dashboard shows how often ChatGPT mentions a brand and drives clicks to its site, plus “discovery topics” that can point to gaps in what the brand shares.

  • OpenAI first piloted ad-linked agents in September, and brands can now pay to make their agent the landing spot for ads in ChatGPT, with each paid spot labeled.

Why it matters: Brands used to fight for a spot in Google’s results, and in the AI era, that’s shifted to getting name-dropped by the assistants themselves. Companies were mostly guessing what ChatGPT said about them or paying outside specialists to find out. OAI just handed them that visibility directly, plus a one-on-one line to potential customers right inside the chat.

TOGETHER WITH MEMOKET

🗓️ Your conversations, now in Apple Calendar

The Rundown: Memoket Gem is an AI wristband that captures conversations with one press and turns them into summaries, action items, and connected memory. Now with Apple Calendar integration: connect in the Memoket iPhone app to automatically sync new recordings as calendar events.

With Memoket, you can:

  • Find recordings by when the conversation happened

  • Revisit decisions and context across conversations

  • Bring relevant memories into ChatGPT and Claude

  • Use the app on your Apple Watch, coming this month

Discover Memoket Gem.

ANTHROPIC

🗄️ Anthropic stretches Claude across the office

Image source: Anthropic

The Rundown: Anthropic just rolled out Claude Sheets and Whiteboards in beta — spreadsheets and shared boards Claude builds alongside a team — while making its Claude Data analytics tool generally available and announcing Claude Meetings, an assistant that sits in on video calls.

The details:

  • Sheets can build a working spreadsheet with formulas via prompt and export it to Excel, while Whiteboards maps a plan onto a shared board for a team to edit.

  • Claude Data, originally named Dashboards when it entered beta in October, turns company metrics into narrated videos and visual data stories.

  • Product lead Nicholas Lin said Claude joins nearly every Anthropic meeting after months of testing, with a Google Meet beta coming to Team and Enterprise users.

  • Upgraded connectors, the links between Claude and other work apps, now also open tools like Adobe and Atlassian fully inside Claude without switching platforms.

Why it matters: Claude continues to eat both legacy office software and the newer apps that followed, with spreadsheets, dashboards, and meeting tools now joining Slides, Design, and Docs. The apps it hasn’t rebuilt now open inside Claude anyway, pulling more use into the AI assistant and away from the tools the workday used to run on.

AI TRAINING

🌐 Put your open Chrome tabs to work with AI

The Rundown: In this guide, you’ll use ChatGPT’s updated Chrome extension to compare open pages, check the facts, and group the tabs you need. Start in Chat to read, then use Work for a browser action you approve.

Step-by-step:

  1. Install the official ChatGPT extension from OpenAI and open its side panel. Use a practice Chrome profile with public pages for your first run

  2. Open three pricing pages and tell ChatGPT which tabs to read. Give it your team size, required features, budget, and billing period

  3. Check the comparison against the pages. Confirm the full team cost and leave missing details unverified rather than guessing

  4. Switch to Work where available and ask it to group only those three tabs. Review the list first, then check the actual group in Chrome

  5. Ask for a short recommendation with source links and one question to resolve. Keep trials, purchases, and messages outside the task

Pro tip: Use the same side panel on any article. Select the tab and ask ChatGPT for the main claim, the evidence, and what the author leaves unresolved.

PRESENTED BY GARTNER

🎰 Only 1 in 5 AI use cases pays off  

The Rundown: Enterprise AI use cases grew by 400% this year, but not all are delivering ROI. Investment without value only creates bad momentum. These Gartner IT Symposium/Xpo takeaways show what separates mere AI activity from real, measurable results.

What you’ll learn:

  • How to build momentum that compounds value

  • Ways to prevent key risks

  • How to make people your AI safety net

Download the insights.

AI RESEARCH

📆 ‘AI 2027’ authors move up their timelines

Image source: AI Futures Project

The Rundown: The AI Futures Project, the forecasting group behind AI 2027, just moved up its forecast for AI that matches the best human AI researchers up to 2027 — citing AI evaluator METR’s recent outside review of Anthropic’s AI speedup as its biggest reason.

The details:

  • The group’s paper published in 2025 depicted AI rapidly improving itself, but most of the authors later pushed their dates for AI that beats top experts into the 2030s.

  • METR estimated Anthropic now improves about 2x as fast, mostly thanks to AI, a pace the forecasters’ models gave under 4% odds of seeing this early.

  • Ex-OpenAI researcher Daniel Kokotajlo gave the earliest date, a 50-50 chance by May 2027, while the other five forecasters land between August and November.

  • Kokotajlo wrote on X that he is “scared, sad, and angry,” and the group says that if its forecast holds, a pause “should be the top priority for the AI industry.”

Why it matters: AI 2027 is considered one of the more prescient forecasts for how the industry has accelerated, and even its own authors said the pace shown in METR’s report caught them off guard. If their updated projections are as accurate as their old ones, the industry has months, not years, to prepare for the implications of superhuman AI research capabilities.

QUICK HITS

COMMUNITY AI WORKFLOW OF THE DAY

▸ Polly built a caregiver recordkeeping app with Claude

Today’s workflow comes from reader Polly Bouker:

“My son is disabled and receives state funding for caregiving. The program requires daily records of what was done, whether he met his goals, and any behavioral or health issues. A program coordinator reviews these periodically, and an auditor may review them too. I used Claude to write the code for a web app built with Google tools that handles this recordkeeping.

Each day, caregivers open the app and check off each item on my son’s daily task list, which he completes with their help. The app writes the required daily summary from those check-offs and adds goal tracking. Everything goes into a printable report for the coordinator or an auditor.

My son has his own view showing how much of his list is checked off and how close he is to his favorite reward. Because he is motivated to see that he has earned the reward, he reminds the caregivers to complete their part.”

items.title: Anthropic says ‘pacing, not pausing’ with Fable 5.2
items.content:
Read Online | Sign Up | Advertise

Good morning, {{ first_name | AI enthusiasts }}, and welcome to our 5,334 new readers. Anthropic spent the fall telling the AI industry to pace itself. The company’s first look at what that means just arrived, and the result still sits comfortably at the top of the leaderboards.

Fable 5.2 is cheaper, faster, and strong enough to bump Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon before the public even got to try it. If this is Anthropic’s slow lane, it still looks faster than the rest of the industry can keep up with.

In today’s AI rundown:

  • Anthropic’s Fable 5.2 leads the frontier with a price cut

  • Meta undercuts Anthropic, OpenAI on the cost of agents

  • Clean up a messy Excel report with Claude

  • Google adds two more AI chips to its Nvidia fight

LATEST DEVELOPMENTS

ANTHROPIC

🧠 Anthropic’s Fable 5.2 leads the frontier with a price cut

Image source: Artificial Analysis

The Rundown: Anthropic just released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, two cheaper, faster upgrades to its most powerful AI family that take the top spot on Artificial Analysis’ AI leaderboard — and show how CEO Dario Amodei’s call to “pace the frontier” will work.

The details:

  • Fable debuted at No. 1 on Artificial Analysis’ Intelligence Index leaderboard, edging out Google’s still unreleased Gemini 4 Carbon model by 5 points.

  • Mythos is limited to vetted security and life sciences groups, while Fable is the same model with stronger cyber and biology guardrails.

  • Teams of 1,000 Fable agents built an operating system in 8 days and formalized the full proof of a famous math problem in 30 hours, with Opus finishing just 26%.

  • Fable was held near Opus level in certain skills that speed up development, with exec Dianne Penn saying of the slowdown, “We called for pacing, not pausing.”

  • 5.2 is 20% cheaper and as much as 30% faster than 5.1, though at $8 in / $40 out per million tokens, it still costs twice as much as Opus 5.5.

Why it matters: Google’s run at the top of the leaderboard ended before Carbon was even released, and Anthropic’s pacing certainly doesn’t feel like a slowdown for users without its internal super-models. With OpenAI also expected to release a new model, the bar just moved even higher — and anything less will likely come as a disappointment.

TOGETHER WITH VANTA

🚀 Governance at the speed of AI

The Rundown: Vanta’s AI governance webinar series is six live and on-demand sessions for security and GRC leaders on how to govern AI as fast as you adopt it — covering frameworks, expert Q&A, AI risk, and a live product demo.

In the series, you’ll explore:

  • Frameworks for governing AI from day one

  • Real-time Q&A with Vanta’s GRC experts

  • AI risk, workshops, and a live demo

Register for a session.

META

🔥 Meta undercuts Anthropic, OpenAI on the cost of agents

Image source: Meta

The Rundown: Meta released Muse Ember, the smallest AI model in its lineup, built to handle routine, high-volume steps inside AI agents — with the company saying it matches Anthropic’s budget Claude Haiku 5.5 at roughly one-third of the per-task cost.

The details:

  • Ember tied Haiku 5.5 at 36 on AA’s Intelligence Index, while beating out OpenAI’s comparable GPT-6 Luna (28) by a wide margin.

  • Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang said Ember is meant to pair with the larger Muse Wonder, writing that “wonder can plan, ember can handle the volume.”

  • Ember’s price matches both rivals, with savings coming from using fewer tokens per job and an average test task running $0.14 on Ember and $0.41 on Haiku.

  • Meta trained Ember using its larger Muse Wonder Full, the first model built that way, and said “even more efficient models” are in training.

Why it matters: Meta shipped its first Muse model in April, and it now has answers for every tier Anthropic and OpenAI sell, from the near-frontier down to the bargain bin. Add in a new report of a sales push through the consulting giants those two already use, and Meta’s 2026 consumer success might soon touch the enterprise end of the AI pool.

AI TRAINING

📊 Clean up a messy Excel report with Claude

The Rundown: In this guide, you’ll use Claude inside Excel to clean up a messy sales export, fix a wrong total, and build a report. You’ll check the numbers and test whether a new order updates the chart.

Step-by-step:

  1. Install the official Claude add-in and open a copy of your workbook. Pro members can use our practice file and keep the reference workbook closed until they finish

  2. Tell Claude what each row means and which orders to count. Ask it to find duplicate rows, missing details, and formula mistakes before changing anything

  3. Approve the fixes on a separate sheet. Keep the original data and ask for a record of each change, including any rows left out

  4. Build a monthly report with formulas and a chart. Check the order count, refunds, and sales total against the source rows

  5. Add a test order and check that the report and chart update. Remove it and confirm the original totals return before saving your finished workbook

Pro tip: A spreadsheet can show a wrong total without showing an error. Ask Claude to explain which rows it counted, then check a few yourself.

PRESENTED BY CUBE.DEV

🧠 How BetterUp gets trusted AI answers with Cube

The Rundown: Cube is the semantic layer for AI. Define metrics and access rules once, let AI build your model, and agents, dashboards and apps get consistent answers. BetterUp’s team uses it to query governed data right in Claude, saying it delivers “reliable results, even if you don’t know exactly the right question to ask.”

With Cube, you can:

  • Model metrics and joins in code, with access policies enforced at query time

  • Connect Claude or ChatGPT over MCP to chat with your governed data

  • Build dashboards without code: a non-technical BetterUp manager built one of its most-used dashboards

See BetterUp’s story, then get started with no card required.

GOOGLE

💾 Google adds two more AI chips to its Nvidia fight

Image source: Google

The Rundown: Google announced the TPU 8tx and 8i Max, two specialized versions of its custom AI chips arriving next year, with one built to keep sensitive data safe and the other to handle jobs needing an AI to hold huge amounts of information at once.

The details:

  • Google began selling TPUs to other companies this year and has nearly 100 customers, including Anthropic and Apple, with every available chip spoken for.

  • Data stays encrypted on the 8tx even while an AI model is working on it, a step where it normally sits exposed, with governments and regulated firms as targets.

  • The 8i Max joins two chips as one unit to double processing power and memory speed, for AI agents that must keep an entire codebase or long video in view.

  • “The future is going to be about specialization,” Amin Vahdat, who runs Google’s chip work, told Bloomberg, expecting both to reach customers next year.

Why it matters: Google couldn’t have asked for better timing, rolling out two Nvidia challengers the day after Jensen Huang’s apology and his board’s probe. While Google still seems constrained in how much it can build, the demand is clearly there — making it interesting both as a chip supplier and as an AI lab that owns its entire stack.

QUICK HITS

COMMUNITY AI WORKFLOW OF THE DAY

▸ A Rundown reader built an AI running coach for a friend

Today’s workflow comes from an anonymous Rundown reader:

“My friend is a competitive runner who wears a Garmin watch for every session. Each run produces a spreadsheet’s worth of data: pace, heart rate, cadence, ground contact time, vertical oscillation, and power, broken down lap by lap. Garmin Connect shows the numbers but can't explain them. It can't tell him whether a late pace drop came from fatigue, wind, or a hill, or whether his fitness is really improving. I built Stride to add that meaning for runners who already have the data.

Stride runs sports-science-style analysis. Aerobic fitness tracks heart rate within each pace band week over week, so a lower heart rate at the same pace signals improving fitness. The Environment layer adds weather and elevation, so a slow lap into a headwind is judged fairly.

AI Coach sends a structured 30-day summary to Claude, which returns a plain-English brief on trends, environmental factors, and things to watch. What-If answers questions grounded in his own data, such as his likely 5K time on a flat, windless course.”
